ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Muscle will contract when stimulated, and the changes in electric potential inside and outside the muscle cell membrane before and after the muscle is stimulated are the same as the potential changes in nerve fibers. Now take two fresh nerve-muscle specimens, and place the nerve of the left specimen on the muscle of the right specimen; at this time the nerve fiber is connected with the muscle cell (during the experiment the specimens are moistened with physiological saline), as shown in the figure. In the figure, ② and ④ refer to the junctions between nerve fibers and muscle cells; these junctions are similar to synaptic structures. Stimulating ① can cause the right muscle to contract, and the left muscle also contracts along with it. Which muscles will contract if ③ is directly stimulated?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there are two specimens, the left muscle and the right muscle, and a nerve fiber crosses horizontally over the muscles on both sides. Label ④ is located at the contact point between the left muscle and the nerve fiber, and label ② is located at the contact point between the right muscle and the nerve fiber; label ③ is on the nerve fiber connecting the left and right sides, positioned between ④ and ②; label ① is on the nerve fiber to the right of ② on the right side, and there is an arrow labeled “S stimulation” pointing to this area. Reasoning: The question stem states that ② and ④ are junctions between nerve fibers and muscle cells, similar to synaptic structures; stimulating ① can cause the right muscle to contract, and the left muscle also contracts along with it, indicating that excitation on this nerve can conduct and make the corresponding muscle excited through the junction. When ③ is directly stimulated, ③ is on the same nerve fiber, and excitation will conduct along the nerve fiber to both sides: to the left it reaches ④, causing the left muscle to contract; to the right it reaches ②, causing the right muscle to contract. Therefore, directly stimulating ③ will make both the left muscle and the right muscle contract.
